brief: Why most note systems collapse, and what survives

slots.subtitle: Six things that decide whether a note system is thinking or filing, and the point at which most become filing.
slots.item1: Why capture is not the hard part
slots.item2: The weekly pass that makes the rest work
slots.coverNote: The last page is the one the apps do not mention

slots.body: A note you had to open an app to make is a note you did not make. The capture step has to be faster than the thought is fleeting, which in practice means one place, always open, no decisions about where it goes.
slots.p1Body: Sorting at capture time is what stops people capturing.
slots.p2Body: Anything that loads slowly stops being used within a fortnight.
slots.p3Body: Any other metadata is a tax paid at the wrong moment.

slots.body: Capture without review produces an archive, not a system. The weekly pass is the entire mechanism — twenty minutes deciding what to keep, what to connect and what to delete, and the deleting is the part that makes the rest usable.
slots.p1Body: Enough to keep it honest, short enough to actually happen.
slots.p2Body: An archive of everything is searchable by nobody.
slots.p3Body: If you cannot restate it, you did not understand it.

slots.body: Folders force one answer to a question with several. A note that links to three others belongs to all of them, which is closer to how you will actually look for it, and it removes the decision that makes filing systems collapse.
slots.p1Body: Not later. Later never comes, in any system.
slots.p2Body: A link with no reason attached is a dead end in a month.
slots.p3Body: The clusters that form are the real categories.

slots.body: Not what it was about. Notes are found by the phrase you happened to use at the time, which is why titles matter far more than tags and why a note titled with a full sentence is worth ten tagged perfectly.
slots.p1Body: 'Constraints beat mood boards' is findable. 'Design notes' is not.
slots.p2Body: If you cannot find it in ten seconds it does not exist.
slots.p3Body: One page listing what matters, maintained by hand.

slots.body: Notes that never become anything are a hobby with the appearance of work. The measure is not how much is captured or how neatly it is arranged — it is how much of it has left the system and become something somebody else saw.
slots.p1Body: Even badly. The output is what validates the input.
slots.p2Body: Whole categories can be abandoned without cost.
slots.p3Body: Anything untouched for a year was collection, not thinking.

slots.body: Building the system feels like intellectual work and produces nothing. The people who get the most out of notes are usually running something crude and unmaintained, because the returns come from thinking, not from the apparatus around it.
slots.p1Body: A text file that is open beats any structure that is not.
slots.p2Body: Every hour on the system is an hour not spent thinking.
slots.p3Body: Nothing else about a note system is measurable.

slots.body: Not a new system, not a migration, not an evening of research. One pass over what you captured, keeping only what you would want to find again.
slots.closingLine: A crude system you review beats an elegant one you maintain.
slots.signoff: The deleting is what makes the rest usable
